en: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now at that time, a wandering ascetic named Dīrghanakha, a brahmin, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he leaned on his staff before the Blessed One and said this to him:
"Is it true, Master Gautama, that you say: 'The world has karma as its own, karma as its inheritance, karma as its womb, karma as its kin, and karma as its refuge'?"

The Blessed One said: "It is even so, Great Brahmā. I say this: the world has karma as its own, karma as its inheritance, karma as its womb, karma as its kin, and karma as its refuge. The Brāhmaṇa said: "Regarding what you say, what prior karma was performed and accumulated by the Śramaṇa Gautama, by which the Śramaṇa Gautama is endowed with a body like a diamond (*vajra*)? The Blessed One said: "Great Brahmā, in a previous birth, I abandoned the taking of life and abstained from taking life. This is the fruit of that karma."

The brahmin asked: "What former karma was performed and accumulated by the ascetic Gautama, such that the ascetic Gautama has hands with long fingers joined by webs? The Blessed One said: "O great brahmin, in a previous birth, having abandoned taking what is not given, I abstained from taking what is not given. This is the fruit of that karma. The brahmin asked: "What former karma was performed and accumulated by the ascetic Gautama, such that the ascetic Gautama has complete sense faculties and a complete body?"

The Blessed One said: "O Great Brāhmaṇa, in a previous birth, having abandoned sexual misconduct, I abstained from sexual misconduct. This is the fruit of that karma. The Brāhmaṇa asked: "What former karma was performed and accumulated by the Śramaṇa Gautama, such that the Śramaṇa Gautama enjoys three seats—seats that are exhaustive, excellent, and supreme?"

The Blessed One said: "O Great Brāhmaṇa, in a previous birth, having abandoned high and luxurious beds, I abstained from high and luxurious beds; this is the fruit of that karma. The Brāhmaṇa asked: "What former karma was performed and accumulated by the Śramaṇa Gautama, such that the Śramaṇa Gautama covers his entire facial circle with his tongue up to the hairline?"

The Blessed One said: "Great Brāhmaṇa, in a previous birth, having abandoned false speech, I abstained from false speech. This is the fruit of that karma. The Brāhmaṇa asked: "What former karma was performed and accumulated by the Śramaṇa Gautama, such that the Śramaṇa Gautama walks with the stride of a lion?

The Blessed One said: "Great Brāhmaṇa, in a previous birth, having abstained from the occasion of negligence consisting of fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants, this is the fruit of that karma."
The brahmin asked: "What former karma was performed and accumulated by the ascetic Gautama, such that the body of the ascetic Gautama is adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man?

The Blessed One replied: "O great brahmin, in a previous birth, I abstained from the pleasures of dancing, singing, and instrumental music; this is the fruit of that karma. The brahmin asked: "What former karma was performed and accumulated by the ascetic Gautama, such that the body of the ascetic Gautama is anointed with the fragrance of morality?"

The Blessed One said: "O Great Brahmin, in a previous birth, having abandoned the wearing of perfumes, garlands, ointments, cosmetics, and ornaments, I abstained from wearing perfumes, garlands, ointments, cosmetics, and ornaments. This is the fruit of that action."

The brahmin asked: "What former karma was performed and accumulated by the ascetic Gautama, such that the ascetic Gautama is endowed with forty teeth—teeth that are very white, very beautiful, and very bright? The Blessed One said: "Great brahmin, in a previous birth, I abandoned eating at improper times and abstained from eating at improper times. This is the fruit of that karma. The brahmin asked: "What former karma was performed and accumulated by the ascetic Gautama, such that the ascetic Gautama has a head with a prominent uṣṇīṣa?"

The Blessed One said: "O Great Brāhmaṇa, in a previous birth, when I was reborn, I prostrated with my five limbs touching the ground before the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, my teachers, those worthy of offerings, and my mother and father. This is the fruit of that action."

Then the wandering mendicant Dīrghanakha, having set down his staff and water-pot on the ground, said this to the Blessed One: "I go for refuge, Venerable Sir, to the Blessed One, to the Dharma, and to the Saṅgha of monks. From this moment forth, Venerable Sir, for as long as life lasts, I shall observe the noble eightfold *poṣadha*: [abstaining] from killing any living being, from taking what is not given, from unchaste conduct, as well as from divisive speech, from false speech, from intoxicants that cause heedlessness, from drinking [intoxicants], and from eating at improper times."
Today I have desisted from the pleasures of garlands, cosmetics, dance, song, and high beds and seats; I practice the conduct of the Arhats with its eight qualities.
The Blessed One said, "Excellent, excellent, Great Brāhmaṇa! This very thing is what must be done.
Then the wandering mendicant Dīrghanakha, the Great Brāhmaṇa, and that entire assembly—including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
Thus ends the eleventh sūtra, the *Dīrghanakha-paripṛcchā*.
